chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, on the authority of Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Hurayz ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Nine things have been lifted/removed from my nation: error, forgetfulness, what they were forced to do, what they do not know, what they cannot bear, what they were compelled to do, jealousy, good/bad omen, and pondering the whispers (of Satan) regarding creation as long as it is not verbally expressed by the tongue.'
ai.seo_question: What are the nine things exempted from sin in Islam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith elaborates on the legal principle of *raf’ al-hajr* (lifting of burden), distinguishing between external compulsion and internal cognitive states like *waswasa* (whispers) that remain unvoiced. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on intentionality (*niyyah*) and the exemption of the community from minor mental distractions until they manifest in speech or action, reflecting the mercy inherent in divine legislation.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 9-9 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Hurayzibn Abdullah, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “

Nine things have been removed for my nation: error; forgetfulness; an abominable deed done by force; what they do not know about; what they cannot tolerate; what makes them anxious; jealousy; bad omen; and having tempting thoughts about the world’s creation as long as it is not verbally expressed in words.”
